acceptanceClaims: the pre-fix physical race released a preflight-valid successor and the existing dead-owner reconciler against the same partial S6 world, and both physically mutated it
the baseline successor moved part of the q/w veth pair before the reconciler deleted the same world, then failed because its previously validated namespace/link disappeared
the minimal fix separates predecessor provenance from current recovery authority and binds successor claim acquisition to the exact inherited ledger digest
the actual single-host mutex is one per-Run kernel flock; durable claim metadata records provenance but is not trusted as physical authority
while a live successor held the recovery gate, the first reconciler returned skipped-successor-active and independent Host observation proved it made no world mutation
the successor then continued the same partial effect to peer-b-present while holding the claim
successor SIGKILL left durable claim metadata in held state but automatically released the kernel gate, allowing a second reconciler to acquire recovery authority
the second reconciler preserved the exact stale claim in its receipt, closed every declared process and namespace, removed the claim metadata, and left zero physical residuals

baselineFalsifier.successorError: peer-B namespace/link disappeared during concurrent reconciliation

limitations: the accepted mutex is single-host Linux flock and is not evidence for a distributed ownership protocol
only one successor versus one reconciler was physically arbitrated
fairness and priority between multiple successors are unproved
successor-to-successor handoff without crash is unproved
the experiment does not prove generic exactly-once semantics or generic causal-DAG requirements
the accepted Range remains structurally unrouted and does not authorize external or uncontrolled targets
